options: A native, vectorized execution engine written in C++, replacing JVM execution for supported operators
A Spark configuration flag that speeds up any query when enabled
A new file format that replaces Parquet
A separate cluster type used only for machine learning workloads
questions.explain: Photon swaps out the engine actually executing supported operators — it isn't a tuning knob on the existing JVM engine.

questions.q: Which query shapes benefit most from Photon?
options: Scans, aggregations, and joins over large row counts
Python UDFs applying custom row-by-row logic
Queries that touch only a handful of rows
Queries that never read from Delta or Parquet
questions.explain: Photon vectorizes batch-oriented operators like scans, aggregations, and joins — it can't vectorize arbitrary Python UDF code.

questions.q: Why can a single query be partly accelerated by Photon and partly not?
options: Photon rewrites specific operators (scan, filter, aggregate, join, write) individually — unsupported operators like Python UDFs fall back to the JVM within the same plan
Photon only works on the first half of any query plan
Photon acceleration applies to an entire query or not at all, with no partial cases
Photon only runs during off-peak hours
questions.explain: Acceleration is operator-by-operator, not query-by-query — a query mixing an aggregation with a Python UDF gets Photon for the aggregation only.

questions.q: What's the reliable way to confirm a specific operator actually ran on Photon?
options: Check the query profile for a Photon indicator on that operator node
Assume it did, because the cluster's Photon checkbox is enabled
Check the cluster's total memory usage
Check whether the query used a Python UDF anywhere
questions.explain: The cluster config checkbox only says Photon acceleration is available — the query profile shows which operators actually used it.

questions.q: Why doesn't a Python UDF benefit from Photon acceleration?
options: Photon can't vectorize arbitrary Python code, so that step falls back to standard JVM execution
Python UDFs are not allowed to run on Databricks clusters at all
Photon only supports operators written in Scala
Python UDFs always run faster than Photon regardless
questions.explain: Photon's vectorization applies to its own native operator implementations — arbitrary Python logic still executes on the JVM.
